facts.text: Saffire-2 flew on CRS OA-5 (Cygnus) and burned nine smaller samples, each 29 cm x 5 cm.
Samples 5 and 6 were SIBAL fabric; Sample 9 was a 1-cm-thick flat PMMA slab.
Two cameras recorded the burns at 30 frames per second, each imaging just over half of the sample.
The sample was illuminated with a green LED for 0.4 s every 2 s so the pyrolysis char front could be seen.
Pyrolysis front and base were tracked along the sample centerline; pyrolysis length is the distance between them.
In forced concurrent flow (20-25 cm/s) flames reached a quasi-steady state with limiting pyrolysis lengths of about 4-5 cm and spread rates around 2 mm/s.
The thick PMMA sample asymptotically reached a limiting length in microgravity.
